message.content:
Below is a concise summary of key tenant‑rights and responsibilities under Texas law (as of 2026). It’s meant as a quick reference—if you have a particular situation (e.g., eviction notice, repair dispute), consult your local housing agency or attorney for tailored advice. | Area | What You’re Generally Allowed / Required To Do | |------|----------------------------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent if lease says “no pets.”
• Up to two months’ rent if lease allows pets.
• Must return deposit within 30 days after tenancy ends unless landlord lists damages/ unpaid amounts. | | **Habitability & Repairs** | • Landlords must keep premises safe, sanitary, and fit for living (Texas Property Code §92.001–92.006).
• If major repairs aren’t made promptly, tenants can file a complaint with the county clerk or seek court relief. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent due dates set in lease; late fees allowed only if specified in lease and reasonable.
• Tenants cannot refuse payment because they disagree with a clause – disputes resolved through courts or mediation. | | **Entry Rights** | • Landlord needs written notice at least 24 hours before entry, except emergencies. | | **Eviction Process** | • Evictions require proper notice per lease terms and statutory reasons (nonpayment, violation, etc.).
• Notice periods vary: typically 10 days for nonpayment, 30 days for other breaches. | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party may terminate early with written notice respecting lease length or statutory minimums. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Fair Housing Act prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, age, source of income, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, or veteran status. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Tenant has right to live without unreasonable interference from landlord or others. | ### Quick Tips 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully:** All obligations—including pet rules, maintenance duties, and notice requirements—are spelled out there. 2. **Document Everything:** Keep copies of notices, receipts, photos of damage, and communication logs. 3. **Know Local Ordinances:** Some cities add extra protections (rent control, utility regulations) beyond state law. If you suspect a landlord violated your rights, contact the Texas Attorney General’s Office, your city’s code enforcement office, or a local tenant advocacy group. For serious matters like unlawful evictions or habitability issues, consider seeking free or low‑cost legal aid.
